stem: A college has three sections. Section A has 40 students with mean marks 60; Section B has 50 students with mean marks 55; Section C has an unknown number of students with mean marks 48. The mean marks of all students taken together is 53. What is the combined mean marks of Sections A and C only (to two decimals)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Takes the simple unweighted average of the two section means (60 + 48)/2 = 54, ignoring that A and C have different numbers of students (40 and 76).
Averages all three section means equally, (60 + 55 + 48)/3 = 54.33, instead of back-calculating nC and weighting only A and C by their sizes.
Computes the combined mean of A and B, (40*60 + 50*55)/90 = 57.22, instead of A and C as asked.

explanation: First recover the unknown section size from the overall mean: 53*(40+50+nC) = 40*60 + 50*55 + 48*nC gives 5*nC = 380, so nC = 76. Then weight only A and C by their sizes: (40*60 + 76*48)/(40+76) = 6048/116 = 52.14. Averaging the section means directly (54 or 54.33) ignores the sizes, and combining A with B answers the wrong pair.

explanation_sections.punchline: The unknown section size is the hinge: solve 53*(90 + nC) = total marks to get nC = 76, then the A-and-C mean is the size-weighted 6048/116 = 52.14, not a flat average of 60 and 48.
explanation_sections.approach: Model: combined (weighted) mean with one group size back-calculated. Assumption: every mean weights by its own count, so nC must be found before any sub-combination. Recipe in five steps. (1) Overall total marks = 53*(40 + 50 + nC). (2) Set equal to 40*60 + 50*55 + 48*nC = 5150 + 48*nC. (3) Solve 4770 + 53*nC = 5150 + 48*nC, i.e. 5*nC = 380, nC = 76. (4) Marks in A and C = 2400 + 76*48 = 6048 over 116 students. (5) Combined mean = 6048/116 = 52.14.
explanation_sections.lesson: A combined mean is always the sum of (count times mean) divided by the total count; recover any missing group size from the overall mean before combining a subset.
explanation_sections.timing: About 155 seconds: one back-calculation for nC, one weighted mean. Reject 54.00 fast as the equal-weight average of two unequal sections, and 57.22 as the wrong pair (A and B).
